records.reason: Measures m66 at 2/1 with the loading conditions of 49201b5817f204116f7f, whose measured 5/1 endpoints were 47.37/119.31 mL. The current 2/1 prediction is 20.86/46.38. This stronger-eluent anchor tests whether the newly learned late response is appropriately localized in solvent ratio.

Measures m90 at 2/1, matching the 100-uL loading of measured 855832bd4005ac7abdc6 at 5/1. Its predicted 14.31/30.10 mL provides the ester counterpart to the selected m66 ketone point, testing whether their measured 5/1 difference persists at stronger eluent.

Extends m90 to 10/1 at the same loading as its measured 5/1 anchor 855832bd4005ac7abdc6. Together with the selected 2/1 point, the predicted 43.87/84.78 mL tests response curvature after the historical 43.27-mL completion underestimate, rather than learning only a scaffold offset.

Tests m141 at 10/1, predicted at only 14.21/27.29 mL. Its measured 1/1 row de4e10d3a5d448ffcdda and the late m66, m146 and m216 observations motivate checking whether sterically flanked ring nitrogen has a flatter response. The measured m141 reference uses 150 rather than 100 uL.

Introduces tertiary aminoacrylate m19 at 2/1, predicted at 9.50/13.09 mL despite recent nitrogen-family transfer failures. Accessible aliphatic amine interactions with silica are a chemical prior. This tests transfer beyond aromatic nitrogen and complements the ether-acrylate reference 65e1a58ab8e4aa2f1eb6.

Measures m36 at 1/1 with the same 100-uL sample and 900-uL DCM loading as measured 6b7209c2e8154837a8c7 at 2/1. The predicted 8.96/20.39 mL determines whether the recently underestimated aminoacetophenone response falls rapidly at stronger eluent.

Adds m88 at 2/1 below its measured 5/1 row d2921349ba8d9cef15a4 at 26.69/61.83 mL. The current prediction is 9.78/19.01. Comparison with para-amino ester d7f5057912ffbf1231a3 tests positional transfer across ratios, while retaining differences in sample volume and DCM volume.

Tests nitrobenzophenone m177 at 50/1, where the current prediction remains only 11.21/23.34 mL. Its measured 20/1 row aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 was early, unlike late m159 and m178 endpoints. This checks whether m177 remains distinct or has an uncovered transition; sample loadings differ.

Measures methoxybenzophenone m114 at 20/1, extending its measured pure-EA anchor 7ab4e875cad0452c3e13. The predicted 9.46/28.85 mL tests substituent-dependent transfer among benzophenones against the measured m159 curve and selected m178 series.

Introduces para-methoxyacetophenone m115 at 20/1 and 150 uL, predicted at 17.72/38.95 mL. Ortho-methoxy row ebdeaba52880c7eade16 measured 5.08/31.97 at the same ratio and sample volume. This tests local-environment transfer, with PE-versus-DCM loading solvent remaining a confound.

Introduces acetylfluorene m38 at 10/1, predicted at 12.72/32.65 mL. Measured acetylnaphthalene 1a382a7d3a13ed7fb28f and fluorenone c9e08e156472783dee4e supply related carbonyl references. Tests fused-ring and carbonyl-placement transfer, conditional on its larger DCM loading volume.

Introduces ring-expanded ketone m179 at 10/1 alongside m180 under closely matched loading conditions. Their predictions, 16.99/32.09 versus 18.60/34.59 mL, are similar. Tests whether ring size and carbonyl environment preserve a common response beyond measured m180 2/1 anchor 983a604ac43bb4d41238.

Measures m180 at 10/1 to accompany novel m179 and extend measured 983a604ac43bb4d41238 at 2/1. The paired labels make the ring-size comparison interpretable without relying on a predicted reference and constrain the cyclic-ketone solvent response.

Measures ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde m198 at 5/1 below measured fcb9019ffbdb889489f7 at 10/1. Its predicted 9.65/21.56 mL tests whether the historical completion underestimate was localized to weak eluent. Pairing with m193 at 5/1 tests how the isomer difference evolves with ratio.

Measures m120 at 2/1 and 150 uL, matching its measured 5/1 row 20913a7c2077b80b7351. Alongside the selected m119 2/1 point, this tests whether the striking spacer-dependent onset difference at 5/1 is already present under stronger eluent.

Tests the remaining m164 1/1 completion hump, predicted at 21.87 mL, after measured 5df546d9e2f2a29dfc89 rejected the earlier pure-EA spike with V2 of 13.58 mL. Determines whether retraining localized the correction correctly between pure EA and measured 20/1 anchor b7fffd840d208b29776c.

Adds m165 at 20/1 beyond its measured pure-EA row 0bdd638e906bf11a00cb. The predicted 8.05/18.85 mL can be compared with m164's measured 20/1 row b7fffd840d208b29776c, testing correction transfer across conjugated-ketone structures and solvent regimes.

Measures ether-acrylate m20 at 5/1, where the model predicts 17.25/42.24 mL despite only 8.48/13.93 measured at 2/1 in 65e1a58ab8e4aa2f1eb6. Tests whether the ether-containing structure supports a real retention transition or has inherited an excessive response from multifunctional ester families.

Introduces flexible ether-ketone m106 at 20/1, predicted at 10.39/21.42 mL, with low structural similarity to measured molecules. Tests transfer from aromatic ketones and ether-containing carbonyls to a remote ether/CF3 environment, adding moderate-retention coverage outside the newly repaired late families.

Measures unsaturated diester m91 at 20/1, extending measured 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28 at 2/1. The current prediction is only 2.96/9.10 mL. Following the rejected m80 late-transition prediction, this tests the boundary between early diesters and strongly ratio-sensitive carbonyl/ester structures.

Extends sulfoxide m199 to 10/1 at 150 uL, matching measured 1/1 and 5/1 rows 741e52b1633ebf2743f3 and 6bd128bde2e137ea54f3. The predicted 31.82/53.61 mL implies little completion increase beyond 5/1. Tests whether this distinctive acceptor has a plateau or an uncovered later regime.

Introduces diphenylmethane m214 at 5/1, predicted at 8.15/15.47 mL. Measured biphenyl 36767e257ec2c6a901ce and dibenzyl ether 93dec4e70431268ebbc3 provide ordinary-retention references. Constrains inter-ring linker transfer and helps balance corrections learned from polar aromatic structures.

Measures bromoacid m45 under pure EA, predicted at 6.95/16.69 mL, with completion above its 1/1 prediction. Measured 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6 at 5/1 and broad cinnamic-acid row 6802f0b28c5a0c7b4c2a motivate an independent strong-eluent test. Different scaffolds and DCM volumes preclude an acid-class offset.

hypotheses.content: Pyridyl carbonyls and quinolines require scaffold-specific solvent responses. Recent measurements establish substantial retention missed at acquisition, but transfer to sterically flanked pyridines and tertiary aminoacrylates remains untested. Nitrogen presence or TPSA alone is insufficient to assign a shared correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels around newly demonstrated retained regimes can teach graph-by-solvent interactions and prevent a blanket nitrogen correction from degrading ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m66 and m90 approach ordinary retention at 2/1, how does m90 extend to 10/1, and do m141 and m19 follow different responses?

hypotheses.content: The late m178 50/1 observation may arise from a steep solvent-response curve resembling m159, rather than a constant scaffold offset. Substituted benzophenones may have different transition locations. The available m178 endpoint establishes late retention but does not establish the intervening curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched m178 ratio series constrains a large historical failure. Related benzophenones test whether the learned transition depends on the actual graph and recorded loading conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m178 onset and completion begin increasing between 5/1 and 50/1, and do m177 and m114 develop comparable increases?

hypotheses.content: Local functional-group environment can change retention and solvent response even when coarse descriptors are similar. Recent meta/para amino-ester labels are later than the recorded ortho-amino-ester regime, and nitroaldehyde isomers differ at 10/1. Extension to ring size, methoxy position and alcohol branching remains hypothetical; existing comparisons do not isolate mechanisms or remove loading-solvent confounding.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related structural comparisons provide graph-sensitive supervision in ordinary and retained regimes beyond acceptor counts and polarity descriptors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do amino-ester and nitroaldehyde differences persist at adjacent ratios, and do ring-size, methoxy and alcohol-environment comparisons reveal differences absent from current predictions?

hypotheses.content: Onset and completion need separate structure-condition responses. Measured loading contrasts in m11, m159 and m119 mostly preserve completion while onset can move. The m120 5/1 label has much earlier onset than its phenethyl analog but similarly late completion; persistence across loading and stronger eluent remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A loading contrast and matched spacer comparison can teach different adjustments for V1 and V2 instead of fitting broad elution intervals through a common shift. Interval width is a response, not uncertainty.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m120 retain its early-onset/late-completion pattern at 50 uL, and do m119 and m120 already differ in onset at matched 2/1 conditions?

hypotheses.content: The previous pure-EA completion spikes for m164 and m165 were prediction artifacts. Their measured labels support a localized correction, while the current m164 1/1 completion hump and m165 weak-eluent response remain unverified.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Adjacent strong-eluent and weaker-eluent labels test whether retraining repairs a condition-specific failure without imposing an excessive correction across conjugated ketones.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is the m164 1/1 hump measured, and does m165 at 20/1 follow the response suggested by its pure-EA label and related m164 anchor?

hypotheses.content: Similar TPSA and acceptor counts do not justify a uniform late-retention response among esters. The proposed m80 20/1–50/1 rise was rejected by measurement, whereas m13 and m107 exhibit large solvent responses. Weak-eluent m91 and intermediate ether-acrylate m20 behavior test this structural boundary.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Contrasting early diesters with ratio-sensitive multifunctional carbonyls can reduce erroneous transfer of late tails across a recurring ester population.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m91 remain early at 20/1, and is the predicted m20 increase between 2/1 and 5/1 real?

hypotheses.content: The acid records warrant scaffold- and loading-condition-specific completion responses. Cinnamic acid's broad completion cannot safely be transferred to bromoacid m45. The latter's pure-EA behavior is uncovered, and its predicted completion ordering relative to 1/1 is untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An independent acid strong-eluent anchor tests whether endpoint-ordering problems extend beyond conjugated ketones while avoiding an unsupported universal acid correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m45 under pure EA have ordinary short completion or a broader interval consistent with its current nonmonotonic prediction?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes move priority toward previously uncovered graph-condition failures. At acquisition, pyridyl ketone 49201b5817f204116f7f underestimated V2 by 100.53 mL, pyridyl ester 855832bd4005ac7abdc6 by 43.27 mL, and dibenzoyl 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 by 76.19 mL. These are historical errors, not current-model residuals. Current predictions have already changed, so adjacent-condition measurements are more useful than assuming those errors persist unchanged. Amino-ester rows d2921349ba8d9cef15a4 and 3ccd6444c8a55917fbf8 also strengthen concern about functional-group environment transfer. Conversely, 40fd02db79e028fe05a9 and 08155ffdcb0d27576050 reject the proposed m80 weak-eluent transition: measured completions remain about 8 mL. The m164/m165 pure-EA spikes were also rejected, with completions of 13.58 and 9.01 mL in 5df546d9e2f2a29dfc89 and 0bdd638e906bf11a00cb. I therefore reduce further sampling of m80 and test the remaining informative conjugated-ketone gaps. The m159 150-uL series now maps completion from 31.58 through 55.72 to 117.40 mL at 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1. The m11 loading contrasts likewise preserve the large ratio effect with relatively small completion changes. These support molecule-specific curves while reducing the value of more loading points in those families. The m119 observations confirm late 5/1 behavior, while m120 row 20913a7c2077b80b7351 reveals a different onset/completion pattern that warrants a focused loading and spacer comparison. Finally, ordinary completion at m202 5/1 and 100 uL in 86258f5c8ffdb874521f weakens a persistent 100-uL late-loading explanation; the anomalous 10/1 pattern remains unexplained and does not justify a broad family correction.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates labels where the last round changed the scientific picture. The m66/m90 points test transfer and localization of newly demonstrated nitrogen-family retention, while m141 and novel m19 challenge extending that correction to different nitrogen environments. Three matched m178 ratios locate the response underlying a major historical failure; related benzophenones test its structural boundary. Amino and nitro comparisons constrain solvent-dependent local-environment effects. The m120 loading contrast and matched m119/m120 2/1 pair distinguish loading response from spacer-dependent band shape. Cyclic ketones, alcohol branching, methoxy carbonyls, a flexible ether-ketone and a hydrocarbon supply additional transfer tests, including moderate and ordinary predicted retention. Conjugated-ketone, diester and acid probes challenge specific response shapes without assuming conventional solvent-strength expectations must hold for every row. The sulfoxide extension tests a distinct acceptor response with matched measured references. Many supplied candidates repeat condition tuples or add nearly identical loading predictions around already well-mapped families; those offer less learning value than these comparisons. No fixed novelty or uncertainty quota was used. The expected benefit is supervision of reusable structure-by-condition relationships for both endpoints, with ordinary anchors limiting excessive corrections across the broader Row-distribution. Actual improvement must be assessed after retraining.
